src/llama/setup.sh

Shell · Tier B

Build local CUDA llama.cpp tools in an interactive Conda workspace.

Usage

Run the commands from a Conda-enabled shell after reviewing the fixed workspace and architecture assumptions; no --help parser exists.

Inputs

Conda, network access, ~/Desktop/Workspace and a CUDA architecture 86 target; creates the llama Python 3.11 environment.

Side effects

Installs build/CUDA 13.0.2 packages, clones llama.cpp and builds llama-server, llama-cli and llama-bench before listing devices.

Cleanup

The environment, clone and build output persist. This command sequence has no rollback or failure trap.

@see src/vllm/README.md

src/llama/start-can3a-max-ornith1.5-35b-a3b-official-q5-llama-3gpu.sh

Shell · Tier B

Serve cached official Ornith Q5 GGUF through llama.cpp.

Usage

Run with a locally built llama-server and an existing GGUF; the Q5 profile defaults to context 262144 and port 8000.

Inputs

MODEL_FILE or cached model discovery, LLAMA_CPP_DIR/SERVER_BIN, CUDA devices, context/batch/cache controls and SERVER_HOST. Placement uses fixed 32,5,3 tensor split with fit disabled.

Side effects

Executes the local server with Jinja/tool-capable prompting and metrics. The wrapper reads local model/cache paths and does not install a runtime or fetch weights.

Cleanup

The Q5 serving process replaces the shell; terminate that process to release GPU allocations. Existing model files and the llama.cpp build remain.

@see src/vllm/README.md

src/llama/start-can3b-max-ornith1.5-35b-a3b-official-q5-llama-3gpu-spec.sh

Shell · Tier B

Run the local Ornith Q5 server with configurable speculative decoding.

Usage

Requires a cached Q5_K_M GGUF and a llama-server exposing --spec-type; capability detection happens before launch.

Inputs

MODEL_FILE, SERVER_BIN, SPEC_TYPE and speculative/draft controls; inspect the selected ngram mode and three-device placement before starting.

Side effects

Probes the local binary help, validates the selected speculative mode, builds its argument list and execs llama-server on the configured host/port.

Cleanup

No draft model or cache is removed on exit; the server process owns GPU lifetime and its own internal speculation state.

@see src/vllm/README.md
